chunks: Abul ‘Abbās Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Abī Dāwūd Al-Mustariq, from Um Sa’īd Al-Aḥmasiyyah, who said:

I was with Abī ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him) and I had sent someone to rent a donkey for me so that I could go to the graves of the martyrs. He asked me, 'What prevents you from going to the Ziyārah of the Master of the Martyrs?' I asked, 'Who is he?' He replied, 'Ḥusain (peace be upon him).' I asked, 'What is the reward for going to his Ziyārah?' He replied, 'One purified Hajj and ‘Umrah as well as this much reward.' Um Sa’īd added that the Imam extended his arms out and then closed them three times (to explain 'this much reward').
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for visiting Imam Husain (a.s.) according to Imam Sadiq (a.s.)?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) elevates the status of Imam al-Husayn (a.s.) as the preeminent martyr, urging Umm Said to prioritize his shrine over other burial grounds. The promise of 'Hajj and 'Umrah al-Mabrura' signifies that the spiritual merit of visiting him is equivalent to a perfectly accepted pilgrimage, free from minor sins, while the gesture of 'so much goodness' emphasizes the boundless divine favor associated with this act of devotion.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 3. Abul ‘Abbās Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain ibn Abil Khaťťāb, from Abī Dāwūd Al-Mustariq, from Um Sa’īd Al-Aḥmasiyyah, who said:

I was with Abī ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) and I had sent someone to rent a donkey for me so that I could go to the graves of the martyrs (of Uḥud). Imam (a.s.) asked me, “What prevents you from going to the Ziyārah of the Master of the Martyrs?” I asked, “Who is he?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “Ḥusain (a.s.).” I asked, “What is the reward for going to his Ziyārah?” Imam (a.s.) replied, “One purified Hajj and ‘Umrah as well as this much reward.” Um Sa’īd added that the Imam (a.s.) extended his arms out and then closed them three times (to explain ‘this much reward’).
